subject:
Concept art of the Raider, a pirate light frigate in a sci-fi space war game, the player's enemy: a small, aggressive warship about 6 meters long, visibly from another faction than the player's clean military ships. Seen from directly above in a flat top-down orthographic plan view, its nose pointing straight up, centered, the whole ship visible with a wide empty margin around it, on a plain near-black background. A symmetrical but angular, aggressive silhouette that reads at a small size: jagged forward-pointing prongs like mandibles, hard angles, a rough hull of mismatched, patched and scorched armor plates bolted onto a salvaged frame. Engines at the back with glowing red-orange exhausts. The pirates' color: hot red-orange glowing strips and panels, clearly visible from above. No gun turrets or cannons: at most one small, low hardpoint bump near the nose for its single weapon. Even, clear light so every part reads. No text or lettering anywhere.

Clean and neat: one object, whole and readable, on a plain background. Palette: background in deep navy blacks (#0A0F16, #111722, #192130); hull in dark gunmetal and cool steel grays (#4A4D58, #686A79, #97999F), rougher and darker than a clean military ship; light in hot red-orange (#D9482B, #FF7A3D, #FFB27A), the only bright accent. Crisp and sharp everywhere: clean hard edges, fine detail; no haze, no soft focus, no depth-of-field or motion blur. Realistic light, cinematic concept art. No text, no lettering, no numbers, no logos, no interface, no lens flares.
